passages.original: multa alia in Scipionis exitu maxime vitae dieque dicta, morte, funere, sepulcro, in diversum trahunt, ut, cui famae, quibus scriptis adsentiar, non habeam. non de accusatore convenit: alii M.Naevium , alii Petillios diem dixisse scribunt, non de tempore, quo dicta dies sit, non de anno, quo mortuus sit, non ubi mortuus aut elatus sit: alii Romae, alii Literni et mortuum et sepultum. utrobique monumenta ostenduntur et statuae: nam et Literni monumentum monumentoque statua superimposita fuit, quam tempestate disiectam nuper vidimus ipsi, et Romae extra portam Capenam in Scipionum monumento tres statuae sunt, quarum duae P.
passages.english: Many other things in the account of Scipio's end, most of all of his life, of the trial date set for him, of his death, funeral and tomb, pull in different directions, so that I cannot say which tradition, which writings, I should agree with. There is no agreement about the accuser: some write that Marcus Naevius summoned him to trial, others the Petillii; none about the time when the date was set, none about the year in which he died, none about where he died or was carried out for burial: some [say] that he both died and was buried at Rome, others at Liternum. In both places monuments and statues are shown: for at Liternum there was a monument, and a statue set on top of the monument, which we ourselves recently saw thrown down by a storm; and at Rome, outside the Capena Gate, in the monument of the Scipios there are three statues, of which two [are said to be those] of Publius
passages.notes: The phrase 'in Scipionis exitu maxime vitae dieque dicta' is awkward and possibly corrupt; rendered as 'of his life, of the trial date set for him'. The final sentence breaks off mid-name and continues in the following passage ('and Lucius Scipio, the third of the poet Quintus Ennius').
